The desired-state revision adds three concrete resolver/runtime findings: execution.extensions.gitnexus=false is applied after --tools resolution; session health currently treats package presence as healthy while resolution-diagnostics has version/catalog compatibility checks; and extension-state warnings do not consistently prevent unavailable extension tools from being advertised. It also separates this Specialists-local patch train from the existing XTRM R1 Pi v0.84.1 compatibility certification lane, so this epic must not claim full Pi compatibility unless that lane closes independently. source.description:
## PROBLEM
The Serena retirement commit 7053236f removed the active Serena catalog and symbolic file-reader surface but left config/catalog/index.json hard-denying native read, grep, find, and ls whenever GitNexus is considered healthy. The current manifest resolver can therefore strip the only direct file-content reader from GitNexus-backed specialists.

A second verified contract split exists across resolver, diagnostics, and launch. execution.extensions.gitnexus=false is converted to an extension exclusion only after --tools resolution; src/pi/session.ts currently treats global pi-gitnexus package presence as loaded_healthy while resolution-diagnostics.ts has stricter version/catalog-compatibility classification; and resolver extension-state warnings do not consistently prevent unavailable extension tools from being advertised in the effective tool list. bare is a concrete disabled-GitNexus case.

Several prompts also hard-code tool inventories that do not match their resolved harness. The mandatory-rule budget path can drop the complete block above 2000 estimated tokens while runner telemetry still records resolved sections as injected. The published @jaggerxtrm/specialists 3.21.2 artifact predates Serena retirement while current source retains the same version. Pi read returns file content without per-line numbering, so exact file:line claims require an explicit verification contract.

The broader Pi v0.84.1 RPC compatibility programme is already owned by the XTRM Final Completion Campaign and docs/design/pi-v0.84.1-compatibility-audit.md. This epic repairs the Specialists-local runtime and patch-release contracts; it must not imply full Pi v0.84.1 end-to-end compatibility certification unless that separate lane has actually passed.

## SUCCESS
Native read remains available for direct file inspection. grep/find/ls may remain hard-denied only when the replacement GitNexus extension is enabled, loaded healthy, and catalog-compatible. Disabled, missing, unhealthy, or catalog-mismatched GitNexus restores the intended native fallback and is not advertised as an effective runtime tool. Resolver, launch, and diagnostics derive from one coherent effective extension state.

Specialist prompts consume or accurately reflect a runtime-derived resolved tool contract rather than relying on stale static tool inventories. obligations-scanner receives deterministic diff evidence instead of requiring shell capabilities its READ_ONLY harness may not expose.

Mandatory-rule budgeting is deterministic and fail-closed for a non-evictable safety floor; telemetry reports only the sections and token estimate actually sent, including explicit retained/evicted section identity and a payload digest. Published package contents, version metadata, and source agree, with release attestation sufficient to reproduce the packaged runtime contract. Citation behavior is either line-numbered/verified by a supported path or exact line claims are withheld. No active Serena runtime integration returns.

## SCOPE
Cover config/catalog/index.json; manifest resolution; execution.extensions.gitnexus propagation; extension health/version/catalog-compatibility classification; src/pi/session.ts and resolution diagnostics; affected specialist definitions and prompt/runtime tool-contract injection; obligations-scanner diff delivery; unit and integration tests; task-prompt mandatory-rule budgeting; mandatory-rules compiler behavior; runner payload and observability metadata; package/build/release metadata; npm pack and installed-tarball smoke tests; release attestation; and the supported Pi read/citation contract.

## NON_GOALS
Do not reintroduce Serena. Do not redesign GitNexus or replace its graph/search role. Do not redesign Beads or Dolt persistence. Do not reconstruct unavailable historical Hiryuen telemetry. Do not implement the broader Pi v0.84.1 lifecycle remediation, native XTRM harness, AgentSession spike, or RLM work inside this epic; coordinate with those existing programme lanes instead. Do not claim full Pi compatibility from a Specialists-local patch release.

## CONSTRAINTS
Ship backward-compatible patch releases. Preserve native read; keep grep/find/ls preference/denial only where a real healthy replacement exists. Treat release artifacts and effective tool manifests as runtime contracts. Avoid claims based only on package presence or stale graph indexes. Record exact payloads and effective extension state. Use typed Beads dependencies and keep external Pi work explicitly coordinated. If the mandatory safety floor cannot fit its configured budget, abort prompt construction with an actionable error rather than executing without required rules.

## VALIDATION
- [ ] Resolver matrix covers enabled healthy, unhealthy, not-installed, disabled, and version/catalog-mismatched GitNexus plus hard/soft deny modes.
- [ ] execution.extensions.gitnexus=false participates in tool resolution before --tools is emitted; bare is a regression fixture.
- [ ] Effective tool output never advertises disabled/unavailable extension tools and native read survives all eligible tiers.
- [ ] Prompt audit covers all specialist definitions and runtime-derived tool-contract behavior, including obligations-scanner.
- [ ] Over-budget mandatory-rule tests prove deterministic retention, fail-closed safety-floor behavior, exact injected/evicted telemetry, and digest parity.
- [ ] Focused tests, full supported test/build/lint gates, and package smoke tests pass.
- [ ] Packed artifact contains no retired active Serena surface and matches source/version plus release attestation.
- [ ] Citation behavior has a reproducible numbered or verification test and release notes state its limits.
- [ ] Release notes explicitly distinguish Specialists-local patch compatibility from full Pi v0.84.1 compatibility certification.

## OUTPUT
A sequence of reviewed implementation PRs, batched validation work, one or more patch releases, package/runtime attestation evidence, and an explicit residual-risk handoff into the existing XTRM Pi compatibility lane.

## REFERENCES
- Retirement commit: 7053236fc
- Current catalog: config/catalog/index.json
- Resolver: src/specialist/manifest-resolver.ts
- Resolution diagnostics: src/specialist/resolution-diagnostics.ts
- Session/extension launch: src/pi/session.ts
- Prompt contracts: config/specialists/*.specialist.json
- Mandatory rules: src/specialist/mandatory-rules.ts and src/specialist/task-prompt.ts
- Runner/telemetry: src/specialist/runner.ts
- Pi compatibility canon: docs/design/pi-v0.84.1-compatibility-audit.md
- Package baseline: @jaggerxtrm/specialists@3.21.2
- Web verification date: 2026-08-11

source.description:
## PROBLEM
config/catalog/index.json denies read, grep, find, and ls at all four tier defaults. The resolver hard-enforces that deny when it considers GitNexus healthy, removing native read even though GitNexus does not replace arbitrary file-content inspection.

The effective-extension state is also split across layers. resolvePermissionTools() computes --tools before the launcher applies execution.extensions.gitnexus=false, so a specialist can lose native fallbacks based on an extension that will not be loaded. bare is a concrete case. src/pi/session.ts currently classifies pi-gitnexus as loaded_healthy from package.json presence alone, while resolution-diagnostics.ts has version/catalog compatibility logic. Finally, resolveManifestTools() can warn that an extension is unavailable without consistently excluding its tools from the advertised tool list.

## SUCCESS
Native read survives for direct file inspection in every eligible tier. grep/find/ls are hard-denied only when GitNexus is enabled for the specialist, actually loaded healthy, and catalog-compatible. If GitNexus is disabled, not installed, unhealthy, or version/catalog mismatched, its tools are absent from the effective allowlist and native fallbacks are restored.

Resolver, session launch, and diagnostics use one coherent health/compatibility classifier or one shared effective-extension-state contract. execution.extensions.gitnexus=false participates in resolution before --tools is generated. The distinction between requested catalog tools and effective available tools is explicit enough that unavailable tools cannot be presented as runtime capabilities. No Serena package or runtime path is required.

## SCOPE
Update config/catalog/index.json; src/specialist/manifest-resolver.ts; src/specialist/resolution-diagnostics.ts where needed; src/pi/session.ts; and the focused resolver/session/diagnostic tests. Propagate specialist extension enablement/exclusions into resolver input. Cover explorer, overthinker, seconder, reviewer, obligations-scanner, executor, and bare as relevant special cases. Preserve explicit mergeTierPolicy union behavior.

## NON_GOALS
Do not remove GitNexus preference for graph/search work. Do not redesign GitNexus. Do not add a new replacement extension. Do not modify unrelated tier permissions. Do not solve the wider Pi v0.84.1 RPC lifecycle audit in this task.

## CONSTRAINTS
Use the smallest compatible catalog/resolver change that establishes one effective runtime truth. Keep native bash/edit/write behavior unchanged. Preserve hard denial of grep/find/ls only behind verified replacement availability. Do not infer health from package presence alone when version/catalog evidence says otherwise.

## VALIDATION
- [ ] Focused manifest-resolver, session, and resolution-diagnostics tests pass.
- [ ] Healthy enabled GitNexus: read present; grep/find/ls denied according to policy; GitNexus tools present.
- [ ] GitNexus disabled by execution.extensions.gitnexus=false: GitNexus tools absent and native fallbacks restored before --tools emission.
- [ ] not_installed, loaded_unhealthy, unknown, and catalog/version mismatch cases restore fallback and do not advertise unavailable extension tools.
- [ ] bare with globally installed GitNexus resolves to its intended no-GitNexus tool contract.
- [ ] Resolved tool output is checked for every affected specialist.
- [ ] No Serena references are introduced.
- [ ] Full relevant TypeScript test and build gates pass.

## OUTPUT
A reviewed implementation PR with updated resolver/health tests and before/after effective-tool evidence.

## REFERENCES
Retirement commit 7053236fc; config/catalog/index.json; src/specialist/manifest-resolver.ts; src/specialist/resolution-diagnostics.ts; src/pi/session.ts; config/specialists/bare.specialist.json; web verification 2026-08-11.

source.description:
## PROBLEM
src/specialist/task-prompt.ts skips the complete MANDATORY_RULES block when its estimated payload exceeds the 2000-token limit. src/specialist/runner.ts then derives mandatory-rule meta and payload components from the resolved injection object even if that block was not actually appended to the task prompt. The result is both a governance failure mode (all mandatory rules may disappear) and an observability lie (unsent sections may be reported as injected). The historical 3.21.2 artifact magnifies the condition because it still includes retired Serena rule content, but the all-or-nothing defect exists independently of Serena.

## SUCCESS
Mandatory-rule budgeting uses a deterministic section priority policy with an explicit non-evictable safety floor, conceptually MUST_KEEP / IMPORTANT / OPTIONAL or an equivalent documented scheme. The compiler retains sections in deterministic order until the budget is exhausted and reports precisely what was retained and evicted. If the MUST_KEEP safety floor itself cannot fit the configured budget, prompt construction fails closed with an actionable error; the run never proceeds silently without required governance.

Runner telemetry and payload_breakdown are computed from the final injected payload, not from candidate sections. The observable record includes budget_limit, candidate_tokens, injected_tokens, injected_section_ids, evicted_section_ids, an injected payload digest, and an outcome such as full/degraded/impossible. An over-budget fixture never reports unsent sections as injected. Current source and packed artifact use the same rule set and budget policy.

## SCOPE
Update src/specialist/mandatory-rules.ts, src/specialist/task-prompt.ts, and src/specialist/runner.ts plus mandatory-rule, task-prompt, runner, payload, and observability tests. Define and test priority/eviction behavior, the 2000-token boundary, exact-limit and one-token-over cases, empty sections, a single oversized optional section, an oversized MUST_KEEP floor, deterministic ordering, metadata, payload components, and digest calculation.

## NON_GOALS
Do not silently raise the budget. Do not restore serena-cheatsheet. Do not rewrite unrelated rule content. Do not turn all rule sets into one monolithic prompt. Do not alter unrelated telemetry schemas except for the additive fields required to represent actual injection truth.

## CONSTRAINTS
Preserve relative ordering among retained sections. Record only bytes/tokens/sections actually sent. Keep the cap explicit and change it only through an intentional contract update. Critical bead/session/git safety rules must be covered by the non-evictable policy where their current contract requires them. Fail closed rather than execute below the mandatory floor.

## VALIDATION
- [ ] Under-budget fixture injects all sections and reports outcome=full.
- [ ] Over-budget fixture proves deterministic per-section eviction and reports outcome=degraded.
- [ ] Exactly-at-limit and one-token-over-limit cases are deterministic.
- [ ] MUST_KEEP-only overflow aborts prompt construction and reports outcome=impossible; no model session starts.
- [ ] Runner meta and payload_breakdown equal the final injected sections, token estimate, and digest.
- [ ] No evicted/unsent section appears in injected telemetry.
- [ ] Executor and reviewer scenarios preserve their critical governance sets.
- [ ] Full relevant tests, type checks, and build pass.

## OUTPUT
A reviewed runtime/telemetry PR with a deterministic budget compiler, fail-closed safety floor, and exact payload evidence.

## REFERENCES
src/specialist/mandatory-rules.ts; src/specialist/task-prompt.ts; src/specialist/runner.ts; config/mandatory-rules/index.json; config/mandatory-rules; package 3.21.2 audit; web verification 2026-08-11.

## PROBLEM
The published @jaggerxtrm/specialists@3.21.2 release commit c1e660ab predates Serena retirement 7053236f and its package surface contains config/catalog/serena.json, serena-cheatsheet.md, and retired Serena runtime material. Current source still reports version 3.21.2, so source and installed artifact can expose materially different runtime contracts under the same package version. A source-only resolver fix would not repair existing npm installations.

## SUCCESS
The next patch version is built from the corrected source and has one-to-one parity with its release commit. npm pack and temporary-prefix install smoke prove the package contains no retired active Serena surface, contains the corrected catalog/resolver/prompts/rules, and resolves the intended effective tools. Package metadata, CHANGELOG, git tag, artifact version, and source commit agree.

The release candidate emits a compact runtime attestation sufficient to reproduce what was certified: source commit, package version, tarball integrity/checksum where supported, Pi runtime version/range used for the smoke test, catalog digest, resolved-tool-contract fixture digest or equivalent, mandatory-rules digest/policy identity, and the exact validation command set. The attestation explicitly scopes this patch as Specialists-local unless the separate Pi compatibility programme has also closed.

## SCOPE
Inspect package.json, build and package inclusion rules, release scripts, generated assets, CHANGELOG, CI release configuration, and package smoke tooling. Remove stale Serena files from the packed output through source/package corrections. Bump the current version according to repository release policy, producing the next patch after 3.21.2 unless a newer release has landed. Add or extend release-evidence generation only as much as needed to make source/package/runtime parity inspectable.

## NON_GOALS
Do not publish a major release. Do not reintroduce Serena. Do not delete unrelated historical documentation outside the package surface. Do not bypass release/provenance checks. Do not use this package attestation as evidence that every finding in docs/design/pi-v0.84.1-compatibility-audit.md is closed.

## CONSTRAINTS
Use npm pack or repository equivalent before publication. Verify tarball contents and installed behavior in a clean temporary prefix. Keep source and artifact gitHead traceable. Record exact Pi identity used by smoke tests rather than an unbounded latest. Define rollback/yank procedure before publication.

## VALIDATION
- [ ] Version, source commit/gitHead, tag, and CHANGELOG agree.
- [ ] npm pack dry-run and tarball inspection pass.
- [ ] Temporary-prefix install smoke passes.
- [ ] Packed output has no active Serena catalog, mandatory rule, or runtime integration.
- [ ] Corrected resolver, runtime-derived tool contract, prompt, and mandatory-rule behavior are present in the tarball.
- [ ] Runtime attestation records package/tarball identity, Pi identity, catalog/rule/tool-contract fingerprints, and exact validation commands.
- [ ] Release evidence states the compatibility scope and does not overclaim full Pi v0.84.1 certification.

## OUTPUT
A release-ready patch PR, reproducible runtime attestation, and publication handoff for the next 3.21.x patch.

## REFERENCES
@jaggerxtrm/specialists@3.21.2; release commit c1e660ab; package.json; release configuration; retirement commit 7053236fc; docs/design/pi-v0.84.1-compatibility-audit.md; web verification 2026-08-11.

source.description:
## PROBLEM
The supported Pi read implementation returns selected file content and offset/truncation notices but does not decorate every content line with a reliable line number. Specialists and downstream review conventions frequently present file:line evidence as if the line number were tool-grounded. Without a numbered-read path or deterministic verifier, exact line numbers can be model-counted and wrong even when the underlying file content was read correctly.

## SUCCESS
Specialists establishes one explicit citation contract. Exact file:line claims are emitted only when backed by a numbered-read API/helper or a deterministic verification step. When only raw native read content is available, specialists may cite file, symbol, section, or excerpt but must not present an unverified exact line as tool-reported fact. The contract is tested across blank lines, offsets, limits, truncation, and end-of-file boundaries.

Upstream Pi numbered-read support remains a valid improvement path, but it is not the only acceptable release outcome. If upstream support is not available in this patch train, Specialists ships the minimum reliable verifier/guard and documents its limits. Coordination records the supported Pi package/version identity and any upstream issue/PR without making an upstream change a synthetic blocker when local verification is sufficient.

## SCOPE
Verify the current @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent read contract used by the supported runtime. Coordinate upstream if a stable numbered-read surface is appropriate. In Specialists, add the minimum prompt/runtime/helper/test guard needed to distinguish verified exact-line evidence from raw content reads. Update reviewer/obligations evidence guidance where it currently implies exact line numbers are intrinsic to read output. Record supported fallback behavior and release-note language.

## NON_GOALS
Do not fork Pi wholesale. Do not alter unrelated read semantics. Do not require every evidence citation to include an exact line. Do not claim historical Hiryuen examples as locally reproduced evidence. Do not hold the Specialists-local hotfix solely for an upstream feature when a deterministic local verification path satisfies the contract.

## CONSTRAINTS
Treat Pi as an external dependency and pin evidence to the actual supported package/version. Never fabricate or silently infer a line number as though the tool returned it. A fallback must make its reliability boundary explicit.

## VALIDATION
- [ ] Supported Pi read behavior is pinned to an exact package/version or commit evidence.
- [ ] Specialists tests numbered or explicitly verified exact-line reads.
- [ ] Blank-line, offset, limit, truncation, and EOF cases are covered.
- [ ] Raw read-only fixture cannot produce an exact line-number claim without the verification path.
- [ ] Prompt/reviewer guidance does not claim raw read output contains per-line numbers.
- [ ] Release notes state the supported citation behavior and upstream status.

## OUTPUT
A verified citation contract, optional upstream coordination record, and a Specialists compatibility/test PR or explicit documented blocker if no reliable exact-line path can be provided.

## REFERENCES
Current Pi read implementation in @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent; docs/design/pi-v0.84.1-compatibility-audit.md; reviewer and obligations-scanner evidence contracts; web verification 2026-08-11.

## SCRUTINY
high
